subject: Private deployment residency: fallback authorization + preflight decision record
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Kent <laura.kent@acme.com>, ACME IT <it-contact@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME residency questionnaire — clarification and scope

Marcus / team,

ACME sent back the residency questionnaire this morning (attached). Their ask: they want a clear fallback authorization and preflight checklist for switching EU traffic to APAC private deployment in the event of a region outage, plus evidence that logs and keys remain within EU while the primary is in EU.

High level requirements they flagged:
- Primary data plane must remain EU-resident by default; temporary APAC failover allowed only after explicit customer authorization and with clear egress controls.
- KMS keys for customer data must be EU-based; any APAC warm-standby must not be able to decrypt EU keys without a documented, auditable process.
- All failover actions must produce audit entries forwarded to ACME for at least 90 days.
- Legal needs a short decision record listing who can approve a switchover (roles + backup).

They want a preflight checklist we can run with their ops team before any planned switch and a short on-call playbook for an unplanned outage. Can we put together a single decision record + checklist and quick runbook they can sign off on? I started a template attached.

Attachments: acme-residency-questionnaire.xlsx

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi Feldman
Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Kent <laura.kent@acme.com>, ACME IT <it-contact@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME residency questionnaire — clarification and scope

Thanks Naomi — good summary.

Proposal: we capture two approved fallback modes and associated authorization flows in a short decision record:
1) Controlled warm-standby: pre-authorized by customer for a known maintenance window (ACME ops signs off).
   - Network: route switch via customer peering update + outbound egress ACLs to block EU egress.
   - KMS: use EU key with explicit key-wrapping/unwrapping step that requires ACME KMS owner approval (see Karthik notes).
   - Audit: immediate audit event + 90d export.
2) Emergency temporary failover: requires a named approver from ACME (primary + two backups) and Redwood emergency SLA escalation.

Ask for the engineering owners: Karthik, can you draft the technical preflight checklist (BGP/peering, IP blocks, KMS steps, logging replication, and any SNI/cert constraints)?
Hannah, can you draft the compliance decision record template with the approver matrix and retention policy language so Legal has something specific to sign?

I will schedule a 30-minute sync with ACME ops today after we have first drafts.

Marcus
Engineering Program Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Kent <laura.kent@acme.com>, ACME IT <it-contact@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME residency questionnaire — technical preflight notes

Marcus / team — initial technical notes below. I attached a quick network diagram (network-psa-diagram.png).

Preflight checklist (draft):
- BGP / Peering
  - Validate peering sessions (ASN, MD5) and community tags for failover path.
  - Confirm ACME will update edge routing to prefer APAC prefix on failover window.
- IP Whitelisting
  - Provide final egress IP set for APAC cluster; ACME to whitelist.
- KMS / Key Residency
  - EU KMS holds customer data keys. APAC cluster will store encrypted key-wrapping keys that cannot decrypt EU data without a custodial unwrapping operation that is gated (customer signs a single-use approval token).
  - We will log all KMS unwrap requests to an immutable audit S3 (EU region) and forward a signed digest to ACME.
- Certificates / TLS
  - APAC nodes will use the same SANs and certs; ensure ACME CDN / edge accepts the APAC origin without re-issuing certs.
- Logging and Audit
  - Streaming of logs to EU analytics must be suspended during failover; we will queue then forward after failback unless ACME requests continuous remote shipping.
- Service limitations
  - Latency-sensitive operations (real-time scoring) may degrade under APAC warm-standby — document expected P95 delta.

Attachment: network-psa-diagram.png

I'll turn this into a checklist spreadsheet and flag any gating items for provisioning.

-karthik
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Kent <laura.kent@acme.com>, ACME IT <it-contact@acme.com>, Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME residency questionnaire — compliance decision record draft

Attaching a short decision record template and a residency fallback checklist (residency-fallback-checklist.xlsx). Key compliance points to include:
- Approver matrix: who can trigger planned vs emergency failover. I propose: ACME Primary Ops Lead (Laura Kent) + ACME Security Lead, with Redwood Sr. Engineering Director as the on-call technical approver for emergency escalation. Include an alternate if primary is unreachable (second contact).
- Audit evidence: every failover must generate an immutable audit event with timestamp, approver, and runbook version; Redwood will push the compressed audit bundle to ACME S3 EU with SHA256 checksum.
- Retention & access: ACME retains audit bundles for 90 days; compliance/legal may request longer.
- Post-failover review: 48-hour incident review meeting, RCA and confirmation of data placement.

If Legal wants stronger language (e.g., never decrypt EU keys in APAC without explicit legal concurrence) we need them on the thread.

Attachment: residency-fallback-checklist.xlsx

Hannah
Sr. Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Kent <laura.kent@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME IT <it-contact@acme.com>, Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private deployment residency: fallback authorization + preflight decision record

Thanks for the quick responses and the templates — useful. A few clarifying questions from ACME: 
1) Timeline — can you provide a proposed timeline for a planned warm-standby test (preflight + test switch) and the expected P95 delta for inference latency? We need that for our ops calendar.
2) SOC2 snapshot — can you provide a small extract showing our private deployment (control mappings) so our auditors accept the approach?
3) Emergency auth — the named approver approach is fine; can Redwood provide the mechanism for the single-use approval token you mentioned for KMS unwrap? We prefer an automated, auditable flow (email-based approvals are noisy).

If you can push a single consolidated Decision Record + Checklist + a 30-minute window for a test next week, we can move this to Legal for signature.

Laura
Head of Ops, ACME Financial Services
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Kent <laura.kent@acme.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME IT <it-contact@acme.com>, Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Decision record + next steps (Action items for today's sync)

Laura / ACME team — summary and proposed next steps (short decision record in Confluence):

Decision summary (approved in principle pending Legal sign-off):
- Mode: Controlled warm-standby in APAC for EU primary with explicit customer authorization required for both planned and emergency failover.
- Authorization: Planned - ACME Ops sign-off. Emergency - ACME named approver + Redwood on-call technical approval.
- KMS: EU-resident keys remain single source of truth. APAC warm-standby will only hold wrapped keys; unwrap requires single-use approval token (automated HSM-triggered process).
- Audit & retention: All approval and unwrap events logged and pushed to ACME EU S3 with 90d retention by default.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Karthik: Produce final technical preflight checklist + IP lists + network diagram for ACME (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- Hannah: Publish the Decision Record template in Confluence and add approver matrix + retention language (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- Naomi: Package SOC2 control extract relevant to private deployment; pointer to control IDs for audit (ETA: Tue 05 Oct).
- Marcus: Run 30-minute sync with ACME ops to walk checklist (I'll propose 09:00 BST next Wednesday).

Next meeting: I'll send an invite once Karthik/Hannah have first drafts. Please review the Confluence page once it's up: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRV/ACME+Residency+Decision+Record

Attachments for ACME: soc2-snapshot.pdf (extract), residency-fallback-checklist.xlsx

Marcus Lin
Engineering Program Lead, Private Deployments
